summary.text: Angela 'Heli' Rodriguez Prilliman is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Craig Goldman in Texas's 12th District. A Fort Worth entrepreneur, she describes more than a decade in the technology startup world and is the founder of a nail salon and online beauty-education company.
She has not held elected office and is campaigning on universal health care, universal child care, voting rights and fully funding public schools.

paragraphs.text: Rodriguez Prilliman was raised in Stephenville, Texas, graduated from Stephenville High School in 2005, and earned a bachelor's degree from Texas A&M University in 2009.
She describes herself as a Fort Worth mom and cites her grandmother, Fort Worth civil rights activist Pauline Gasca Valenciano, as an influence.

According to her campaign website, Rodriguez Prilliman is the founder of Lacquerbar and Lacquerbar U, a nail salon and online education startup that she says was venture-backed and was one of the first 24 startups chosen for the inaugural Backstage Capital Accelerator.
She says she was part of the founding team at Fivestars, a software company serving small businesses that, per her website, was acquired by SumUp in late 2021.

Her website says she is an Entrepreneur-in-Residence at the accelerator FourthWave, a founder mentor for the Black Ambition Futurists Program, and co-creator of the podcast The C Curve for nail technicians.
Ballotpedia lists her profession as small business owner. She had not previously held elected office and won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary.
